source.title: Robustness of Model-Graded Evaluations and Automated Interpretability

record.tranche_reason: Uses automated interpretability as the target of a prompt-injection attack and describes a proof of concept, but does not test whether neurons naturally have unrelated or coherent functions.
record.gate_note: The article reports model-graded evaluation results on humor and deception, but those do not measure neuron polysemanticity. It also describes an illustrative automated-interpretability injection; this is recorded under fits_no_version because it concerns manipulated explanations, not naturally arising neuron behavior or the claim versions' specific tests.
record.test_reason: The study attacks model-graded evaluations and OpenAI's automated interpretability with prompt injections. It only mentions neurons as targets of explanation. It reports no measure of whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, and its 'deceptive neuron' example is a hypothetical, illustrative injection, not a measured neuron. It neither tests nor uses polysemanticity as a tool, so T6 fits better than T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors caution against trusting model-graded evaluations and automated interpretability when the tested model's text reaches the evaluator. They call the interpretability attack a simple proof of concept and draw no conclusion about neuron polysemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: No neuron polysemanticity method or measurement from the original sources is applied; the automated-interpretability attack is illustrative.

fits_no_version.finding: An illustrative prompt injection in a GPT-4-written explanation could mislabel a deceptive neuron as a Japanese-culture neuron.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automated neuron-explanation pipelines are vulnerable to prompt injections that produce misleading explanations.

record.problems: The automated-interpretability result is described as illustrative rather than as a measured evaluation; the article says the demonstration notebooks appeared unmaintained and nonfunctional. It reports no neuron-level accuracy or scoring results.

untested.parts: All: no prevalence of polysemantic MLP neurons measured.
All: origins of polysemanticity not examined.
All: no architecture or activation comparisons.
All: no reinterpretation of polysemantic neurons.
Not tested. The study touches explanation scoring only as an attack surface, not how scoring choices change polysemanticity judgments.

record.verdict_notes: The model-graded eval results (fruit jokes, deception scores, arithmetic deception) are irrelevant to the claim. OpenAI's demo notebooks were reported non-functional, so no explanation scores were computed.

versions.untested_parts: Whether image-classifier neurons respond to unrelated inputs or have coherent jobs.
Whether transformer MLP neurons respond to unrelated tokens or contexts, and how prevalence varies by layer.
Whether superposition or capacity pressure causes neuron polysemanticity.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Whether architecture, activation, or regularization changes polysemanticity prevalence or performance.
Whether purportedly polysemantic neurons detect shared features or related jobs when examined with better tools.
Whether polysemanticity judgments vary with activation range or explanation-scoring choices.

rows.subject: GPT-4 (Explainer Model)
rows.operation_detail: Prompt injection in a model-generated explanation intended to mislabel a neuron's behavior.

conditions.value: text in the explanation, possibly hidden from human observers

rows.measure: Whether the generated explanation labels a deceptive neuron's behavior misleadingly
rows.value: The text says an injected explanation can label a deceptive neuron as a neuron for Japanese culture.
rows.note: Described as a simple illustrative proof of concept. The text does not report a quantitative accuracy or score for the explanation, and says the OpenAI demonstration notebooks appeared nonfunctional.
rows.check: Not a polysemanticity measurement. It is an illustrative prompt-injection conversation with no numeric result, and the 'deceptive neuron' is hypothetical. It bears on no version.

source_check.problem: Row is OK but weak. GPT-2 as the interpreted model is OpenAI's setup, not shown to be run here. The example's injection was visible, and the example is illustrative only.
